## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge because it holds the wrong value. It is set to the `started` event's timestamp, so a process that is still running looks finished. A process that started and was then cleared gets NULL. The schema description also contradicts this logic: it calls the value a finish time and says NULL means the process was never started. The source table allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared` event types, so this column cannot represent a finish time as written.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — For process 20 in `sources/process_events.sql:9`, whose only event is `started`, `finished_at` is `'2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'`. That is when the process started, and the process's `state` is still `started`, so a running process is reported as finished. The expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` copies the start time into a column named and documented as the finish time. The event-type check in `sources/process_events.sql:4` (`'created', 'started', 'cleared'`) has no finish event to take a timestamp from. One option is to rename the column to `started_at` and fill it from the most recent `started` event instead of the latest event only. The other is to define which event marks a process as finished (for example `cleared`) and use that event's `occurred_at`. — Anyone who filters on `finished_at is not null` will count running processes as completed and get wrong durations and completion times.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — For process 30 (`started` at event 3, then `cleared` at event 4 in `sources/process_events.sql:10-11`), `finished_at` is NULL. The description says "NULL means the process has never been started", but this process was started. The SQL at `models/processes.sql:10` returns a non-NULL value only when the latest event is `started`, so NULL also covers processes that were started and then cleared. Line 11, "Timestamp when the process finished.", conflicts with the same expression, which takes the `started` event's time. Update the description to match the corrected column logic, so that it says exactly which event fills the column and which states produce NULL. — Readers of the schema catalog will treat cleared processes as never started, and running processes as finished.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The `latest_event` CTE and its `recency = 1` filter are unchanged, so the model still returns one row per process, as the PR description says.
- The new column is documented in `models/schema.yml` in the same change that adds it.
